panels.title: Target Services Online/Offline Status
panels.description: 0 = Prometheus could not scrape the target. The Django tiles count the prod backend or the dev one, whichever this box runs. A tile showing a raw job name is a scrape target with no friendly name yet.

panels.title: Request Rate
panels.description: All Django jobs combined, counted before any middleware runs.

panels.title: Error Rate (5xx)
panels.description: clamp_min keeps the ratio defined when there is no traffic.

panels.title: Firing Alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing in Prometheus right now. The Alerts row below lists them.

panels.title: Unhealthy Containers
panels.description: Running containers whose Docker healthcheck reports unhealthy. No data means the docker-state sidecar is not running.

panels.title: Containers Down
panels.description: Containers with restart: always / unless-stopped that are not running. One-shots such as probe-tools are excluded.

panels.title: Celery Queue
panels.description: Tasks waiting for a worker. Climbing and not draining means the workers are down, stuck or outpaced.

panels.title: Celery Workers Online
panels.description: Workers that sent a heartbeat in the last minute, via celery-exporter. 0 means queued tasks are not being processed.

panels.title: Firing Now
panels.description: Every alert Prometheus is firing, with its labels. Empty is the goal. Messages for these go out through Alertmanager.

panels.title: Alert Timeline
panels.description: When each alert fired and for how long, across the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: Notifications Sent / Failed (last hour)
panels.description: Per channel. A channel that is not configured in .env sends nothing and shows flat zero. Any failed line: check the ALERT_* credentials and `docker logs alertmanager-voicebot`.

panels.title: Prometheus -> Alertmanager
panels.description: Alerts handed from Prometheus to Alertmanager. Errors or drops mean Prometheus cannot reach Alertmanager, so nothing is being sent. Flat zero everywhere with alerts firing means Prometheus is running stale config: `docker compose restart prometheus`.

panels.title: HTTP Request Rate by Service
panels.description: WSGI counts all four gunicorn workers through the multiprocess registry; ASGI is a single daphne process.

panels.title: Error Ratio by Service
panels.description: Share of responses that are errors, per backend. 5xx is the server's fault and what the error-rate alerts watch; a 4xx spike is usually a client or auth problem (expired tokens, bad input).

panels.title: Requests by Transport
panels.description: http vs websocket. Websocket traffic only appears on the ASGI job.

panels.title: Unhandled Exceptions by Type
panels.description: Exceptions that escaped the view. A non-zero line here is always worth investigating.

panels.title: Top 15 Error Responses by View
panels.description: 4xx and 5xx broken down by the view that produced them.

panels.title: Middleware Overhead
panels.description: The gap between these two lines is time spent in the middleware chain rather than in your view.

panels.title: Requests with Unknown Latency
panels.description: Requests the middleware could not time, usually because an earlier middleware short-circuited the chain.

panels.title: Query Execution Rate
panels.description: Statements issued through Django's instrumented postgresql backend.

panels.title: New DB Connections
panels.description: High and steady means connections are not being reused; check CONN_MAX_AGE against PgBouncer's transaction pooling.

panels.title: Workers Online
panels.description: Workers that sent a heartbeat in the last minute. A drop to 0 fires CeleryNoWorkersOnline. A deploy briefly shows the old and new container overlapping.

panels.title: Tasks Running per Worker
panels.description: Tasks executing right now. Pinned at the worker's concurrency while the queue grows means the worker is saturated.

panels.title: Queue Length (waiting tasks)
panels.description: Length of the Celery broker list in Redis db2. Brief spikes that drain are normal; above 100 for 15 minutes fires CeleryQueueBacklog.

panels.title: Task Throughput by State
panels.description: Tasks per minute at each stage. sent is published by web and beat, received/started by the workers. received well above succeeded + failed for long means tasks are piling up or hanging.

panels.title: Failure Ratio by Task
panels.description: Share of each task's runs that failed, over 5 minutes. Only tasks with failures appear. 10%+ with 3 or more failures in 15 minutes fires CeleryTaskFailing.

panels.title: Task Runtime p95 by Task
panels.description: Every completed run, from the exporter's histogram (buckets up to 30 minutes). A task whose line keeps rising is heading for a timeout.

panels.title: Top 15 Tasks by Runs (last hour)
panels.description: Where the workers' time goes.

panels.title: Failures by Task & Exception (24h)
panels.description: Every failing task with the exception it raised. Empty is the goal. The full error text is in Recent Task Failures below.

panels.title: Beat: Tasks Dispatched (from logs)
panels.description: Periodic tasks celery beat sent per minute, from its log. A flat zero where there used to be a steady pattern means beat has stopped scheduling.

panels.title: Recent Task Failures
panels.description: The exception each failed task raised, from the worker log. Expand a line for the full traceback context.

panels.title: Connection Utilization
panels.description: Server-side backends against max_connections.

panels.title: Server Backends (behind PgBouncer)
panels.description: Django connects through PgBouncer in transaction mode, so this tracks the server-side pool, not client connections. Its size is the Azure server parameter pgbouncer.default_pool_size in production, DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE on the local pgbouncer container.

panels.title: Connections by State
panels.description: idle in transaction is the one to watch: a connection holding a transaction open while doing nothing keeps its locks and blocks vacuum. It should sit at or near zero.

panels.title: Longest Open Transaction
panels.description: Age of the oldest transaction in each state. Minutes-long values on active or idle in transaction point at a stuck request or task.

panels.title: Shared Buffer Hit Ratio
panels.description: Sustained below ~95% usually means shared_buffers is too small for the working set.

panels.title: Tuple Operations
panels.description: returned >> fetched is the signature of sequential scans.

panels.title: Temp File Usage
panels.description: Queries spilling to disk because work_mem was not enough.

panels.title: Top 15 Tables by Sequentially Scanned Rows
panels.description: Rows per second read by full-table scans. A large table near the top is usually missing an index for a hot query; small lookup tables here are normal.

panels.title: Top 15 Tables by Dead Rows
panels.description: Rows deleted or updated but not yet vacuumed. A table that stays high is bloating: autovacuum is not keeping up with its churn.

panels.title: Memory Utilization
panels.description: Against the 256mb maxmemory set in docker-compose/cache.yml. At the cap the volatile-lru policy starts evicting.

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Blocked clients are waiting on BLPOP and similar -- expected with Celery, which long-polls its broker list.

panels.title: Keys per Database
panels.description: db2 holds the Celery broker queue and task results, so its key count is not the backlog; see Queue Length in the Celery row.

panels.title: Evictions & Expirations
panels.description: Sustained eviction means the 256mb cap is too small for the working set -- cache entries are being thrown away early.

panels.title: CPU Usage by Container
panels.description: Percent of a single core. 100% means one core fully saturated.

panels.title: Memory Working Set by Container
panels.description: Working set, not RSS -- this is the number the OOM killer uses. It includes kernel file cache charged to the container, so it can run far above what the process uses (cadvisor itself shows hundreds of MB for ~20 MB of RSS); compare with the RSS panel.

panels.title: Memory RSS by Container
panels.description: Memory the processes actually hold, without reclaimable cache. Steady growth here, not in the working set, is a real leak.

panels.title: Container Health
panels.description: Docker healthcheck status over time, for running containers that define one. Red is what ContainerUnhealthy alerts on.

panels.title: Container Running State
panels.description: Containers meant to stay up (restart: always / unless-stopped). Red is what ContainerNotRunning alerts on.

panels.title: Out-of-Memory Kills (24h)
panels.description: Processes the kernel killed for running out of memory, per container. Empty is the goal; any row means that container needs more memory or has a leak.

panels.title: Container Restarts (last hour)
panels.description: Restarts Docker made under the restart policy, i.e. crashes. Deploys recreate containers and do not count. Empty is the goal; 3+ in 15 minutes fires ContainerRestartLoop.

panels.title: Root Disk Used
panels.description: --path.rootfs strips the /host/root bind mount prefix, so the host root filesystem reports as /.

panels.title: CPU by Mode
panels.description: iowait climbing while user stays flat points at disk, not CPU.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: swap used climbing means RAM ran short and the host is paging; expect latency to follow.

panels.title: Host Network
panels.description: Physical interfaces only; veth and bridge devices double-count container traffic.

panels.title: Prometheus Storage
panels.description: On-disk metrics against --storage.tsdb.retention.size. At the cap the oldest data is deleted early, before the 30d time limit.

panels.title: Active Series
panels.description: Time series Prometheus holds in memory; its RAM grows with this. A sudden jump usually means a new label with many values.

panels.title: Loki Ingestion
panels.description: Log lines arriving from Alloy. Dropping to zero means logs have stopped flowing and the log panels below are going stale.

panels.title: Rule Evaluation Failures
panels.description: Alert rules that errored instead of evaluating. A rule that cannot evaluate can never fire, so anything above zero means an alert is silently off.

panels.title: Log Volume by Service
panels.description: Lines per minute. A sudden step usually precedes an incident.

panels.title: Error Log Rate by Service
panels.description: Case-insensitive match on error/exception/traceback/critical/fatal across the app containers.

panels.title: Recent Errors (all app containers)
panels.description: Live tail. Click a line to expand its labels and jump to that container's full stream.
